task_language: put the frying pan under the cabinet shelf

subtasks.name: pick(frying_pan)
subtasks.outcome: never attempted: the white bowl is picked instead

subtasks.name: place(frying_pan, cabinet_shelf, under)
subtasks.outcome: never attempted (the bowl is taken to the top of the cabinet, not under the shelf)

behaviour_summary: pi0 picks the white bowl (~80), carries it to the top-front edge of the cabinet (140-220) where it falls to the table beside the pan (~240); the arm then moves out of the camera view to the right and stays out of view until timeout (260-409).

failures.mode_definition: pi0 approaches, grasps and manipulates a non-instructed object in the scene instead of the instructed target object.
hl_remedy: RETREAT(dz=+0.05) then lower and open gripper to set the wrong object back down near its start
REPROMPT('pick up the frying pan and place it under the cabinet shelf')
WATCH(EE approaches the frying pan, 5 s)
on no approach: retry once with VERIFY of the target at pre-grasp, then ESCALATE
failures.prevention: Before allowing gripper closure, VERIFY the object under the gripper is the instructed target (pre-grasp identity check); HALT as soon as the EE descends over a non-target object for 2 frames. Also VERIFY the relation (under vs on top) of the destination before release.
failures.observation: Gripper over the white bowl at 60, bowl in hand at 80-100, carried back (140) then to the cabinet (160-220). Both object and relation are wrong: the bowl is carried to the top of the cabinet, the same behaviour as task41 ('on top of the cabinet').

failures.mode_definition: The object is released at or beyond the edge of the destination surface and falls off onto the surface below.
failures.rl_success_check: bowl resting upright on the top surface of the cabinet, fully inside its footprint
failures.observation: At 200-220 the bowl hangs from the gripper at the front-left (image) corner of the cabinet top; at 240 it is on the table in front of the cabinet, right of the pan. Recorded as LL evidence on a non-instructed object.

notes: After 260 the arm is entirely outside the frame (only the robot base is visible) until the end; idle out of view for ~150 steps. 1 fps cannot tell whether the bowl release was intended.
